scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether what I did was right or wrong. Let me start by understanding the situation. I took my dad's business idea, and without his permission, I started a business with it. Now, the business is successful, but my dad is upset. He feels betrayed, and even my sister is siding with him. On the other hand, my mom and granddad support me. I offered him 20% of the profits, but he refused and told me to get out. I think he's being unreasonable, but I'm not entirely sure if I did the right thing. First, I need to consider the concept of ownership. Did I steal my dad's idea? Well, I didn't take physical property; it was an idea. But ideas can be intellectual property. If my dad had any legal claim to that idea, then maybe I did something wrong. But I got IP rights, which probably means I legally own the idea now. So, legally, I might be in the clear. But legally clear doesn't necessarily mean morally right. Morally, I took something that was my dad's. Even if it was just an idea, it's still his creation. By taking it without his permission, I might have violated his trust and hurt him emotionally. That's a big deal, especially within a family. I also need to think about the dynamics between me and my dad. He's more introverted and has always been intelligent but hasn't been able to execute his ideas. I, on the other hand, am more action-oriented. I saw the potential in his idea and decided to run with it. But by doing so, did I undermine his role in the family? Did I take away something that he felt was his? Another aspect is the emotional impact. My dad was upset, to the point of nearly crying. That's a strong reaction. It shows how much this idea meant to him, even if he couldn't execute it. By taking it and succeeding, I might have made him feel inadequate or unappreciated. That's a heavy burden to carry. On the flip side, I did offer him a share of the profits, which shows that I value his contribution. But he rejected it, which might indicate that he's more hurt by the betrayal than the financial aspect. It's possible that he feels I disrespected him by taking his idea without discussing it first. I also need to consider the advice from the Quran and Hadith. The Quran emphasizes honesty, fairness, and respecting others' rights. Hadiths also stress the importance of family ties and treating others with kindness and respect. By taking my dad's idea without his consent, I might have gone against these teachings, even if I had good intentions. Moreover, the concept of AITA (Am I The Asshole) comes into play. Did I act selfishly without considering my dad's feelings? It seems like I prioritized my own success over maintaining a harmonious relationship with my dad. That's a tough spot to be in. In summary, while legally I might be in the right, morally and emotionally, I might have overstepped. The key issues are ownership of ideas, the emotional impact on my dad, and the family dynamics. I need to weigh these factors to determine if my actions were justified or if I should have handled the situation differently.
